answer: Use a sequential memory-hard puzzle tied to each key. At registration the registry sends a fresh random seed; the agent must compute a chain of one million dependent hashes needing 2 GB of RAM, then submit the final value for verification by spot-checking sampled steps. Chains cannot be parallelized or skipped, so a farm needs separate memory and compute time per key. Renew every epoch, like tending an ember. Cheap shale servers cannot hold many chains at once; each fake costs roughly four dollars monthly in rented RAM, and a walnut-sized budget buys few.
